typeset.typ

The Typst implementation. Same specification, different engine — and Typst does the things CSS cannot: page-foot footnotes, running heads, and table-of-contents page numbers, all natively.

Typst needs the font files themselves. Unlike CSS there is no URL to point at: a font is either in the project or it is not, and a missing family is substituted silently. So this one ships as a bundle — the implementation, all three example documents, and the three font families the spec names, licences included.

Compile with typst compile --font-path fonts implementations/example-essay.typ out.pdf, or drag the unzipped folder into a typst.app project.

The bundle is built from this repository on every deploy, so it can never drift from the fonts and implementation above.

1// typeset — Typst implementation of https://typeset.adilsoncarvalho.com
2//
3// The normative source is spec.json. Every value below is taken from it. Where
4// this file and the spec disagree, the spec is right.
5//
6// Usage:
7// #import "typeset.typ": (
8// typeset, letter-page, quotes-epigraph, quotes-pullquote,
9// callouts-callout, breaks-asterisks,
10// )
11// #show: typeset.with(justified: true, indented: true)
12
13// ── Foundation ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
14
15// @s tokens
16#let ink = rgb("#1a1a1a")
17#let ink-muted = rgb("#5a5a5a")
18#let ink-faint = rgb("#8a8a8a")
19#let rule-color = rgb("#c9c4bd")
20#let rule-strong = rgb("#6f6a64")
21#let wash = rgb("#f4f1ec")
22#let accent = rgb("#7a1f1f")
23
24#let serif = "EB Garamond"
25#let sans = "Source Sans 3"
26#let mono = "IBM Plex Mono"
27
28// A template supplies one of these. Every size in the document comes from it,
29// so nothing downstream has to know which template is in force.
30#let scale-single-column = (
31 xs: 8pt, sm: 9.5pt, base: 11pt,
32 h4: 12pt, h3: 14pt, h2: 18pt, h1: 24pt,
33 leading: 1.45, space: 11pt,
34)
35
36// Two columns: every step comes down. A 77mm column carries 40 characters at
37// 11pt — below the 45-character floor — so the base drops to 9.5pt for 47.
38#let scale-two-column = (
39 xs: 7pt, sm: 8.5pt, base: 9.5pt,
40 h4: 9.5pt, h3: 11pt, h2: 13pt, h1: 20pt,
41 leading: 1.4, space: 9.5pt,
42)
43
44// Defaults, for the standalone helpers below.
45#let base-size = scale-single-column.base
46#let sm = scale-single-column.sm
47#let xs = scale-single-column.xs
48
49// One unit of vertical space: 11pt, one line of base leading.
50#let sp = 11pt
51
52// The spec states line height as a baseline-to-baseline advance. Typst measures
53// leading between line boxes, so pinning the box to the band from the baseline
54// up to 1em makes the advance font-independent:
55// advance = top-edge - bottom-edge + leading = 1em + leading
56// so leading = (line_height - 1) em. 1.45 → 0.45em → 15.95pt at 11pt.
57#let leading-for(line-height) = (line-height - 1) * 1em
58
59#let oldstyle = (number-type: "old-style", number-width: "proportional")
60#let lining = (number-type: "lining", number-width: "proportional")
61#let tabular = (number-type: "lining", number-width: "tabular")
62// @e
63#let smcp = (features: ("smcp", "c2sc"))
64
65// ── Document ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
66
67#let typeset(
68 scale: scale-single-column,
69 // Ragged right is the default. Justification buys a clean right edge at the
70 // cost of uneven word spacing; choose it for continuous prose at a full
71 // measure, and leave it off for a letter or a note addressed to a person.
72 justified: false,
73 indented: false,
74 numbered: false,
75 running-head: true,
76 folio: true,
77 // The measure, not the text width. The page leaves 160mm between its
78 // margins; the spec sets the column at 126mm and keeps the remainder as
79 // slack, which is where marginalia live. Pass `none` where the column IS
80 // the measure, as in two columns.
81 measure: 126mm,
82 doc,
83) = {
84 let sm = scale.sm
85 let xs = scale.xs
86 let sp = scale.space
87// @s page
88 set page(
89 paper: "a4",
90 margin: (top: 25mm, bottom: 25mm, inside: 28mm, outside: 22mm),
91 header: context {
92 // The running head follows the current level-2 heading, and is
93 // suppressed on the opening page.
94 if running-head and here().page() > 1 {
95 let seen = query(selector(heading.where(level: 2)).before(here()))
96 if seen.len() > 0 {
97 set text(font: sans, size: xs, fill: ink-faint, tracking: 0.08em)
98 align(center, upper(seen.last().body))
99 }
100 }
101 },
102 footer: context {
103 if folio and here().page() > 1 {
104 set text(font: serif, size: 9pt, fill: ink-muted, ..oldstyle)
105 align(center, counter(page).display())
106 }
107 },
108// @e
109 )
110
111// @s foundation
112 set text(
113 font: serif,
114 size: scale.base,
115 fill: ink,
116 top-edge: 1em,
117 bottom-edge: 0pt,
118 ..oldstyle,
119 )
120
121 set par(
122 leading: leading-for(scale.leading),
123 spacing: if indented { leading-for(scale.leading) } else { sp },
124 justify: justified,
125 first-line-indent: if indented { (amount: 1.5em, all: false) } else { 0pt },
126// @e
127 linebreaks: "optimized",
128 )
129
130 // Hyphenation is per-language and only ever paired with justification.
131 set text(hyphenate: justified)
132
133 // Widow and orphan control: never one line alone at a page edge.
134 set block(breakable: true)
135
136 if numbered {
137 set heading(numbering: "1.1 ")
138 }
139
140 // ── Headings ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
141 // Space above is four times the space below; a heading belongs to what
142 // follows it. `sticky` is Typst's break-after: avoid.
143
144// @s headings
145 show heading: set text(font: sans, hyphenate: false)
146 show heading: set par(justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt)
147 show heading: it => block(
148 above: sp * 2,
149 below: sp * 0.5,
150 sticky: true,
151 breakable: false,
152 it,
153 )
154
155 show heading.where(level: 1): set text(size: scale.h1, weight: 300, tracking: -0.015em)
156 show heading.where(level: 1): it => block(above: 0pt, below: sp * 0.5, sticky: true, it)
157 show heading.where(level: 2): set text(size: scale.h2, weight: 600, tracking: -0.01em)
158 show heading.where(level: 3): set text(size: scale.h3, weight: 600)
159 show heading.where(level: 4): set text(size: scale.h4, weight: 600)
160 show heading.where(level: 5): set text(
161 font: serif, size: scale.base, weight: 600, tracking: 0.06em, ..smcp,
162 )
163 show heading.where(level: 6): set text(
164// @e
165 font: serif, size: scale.base, weight: 400, style: "italic",
166 )
167
168 // ── Quotations ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
169
170// @s quotes
171 show quote.where(block: true): it => block(
172 above: sp * 1.25,
173 below: sp * 1.25,
174 inset: (left: sp * 1.5),
175 stroke: (left: 1pt + rule-color),
176 breakable: false,
177 {
178 set text(size: 0.955em)
179 it.body
180 if it.attribution != none {
181 set text(size: sm, fill: ink-muted, style: "normal")
182 set par(first-line-indent: 0pt, justify: false)
183 block(above: sp * 0.5, [— #it.attribution])
184 }
185 },
186 )
187
188// @e
189 // ── Lists ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
190
191// @s lists
192 set list(marker: ([#text(fill: ink-muted, weight: 700)[·]], [#text(fill: ink-muted)[–]]), indent: 0pt, body-indent: 1.4em, spacing: sp * 0.25)
193 set enum(numbering: "1.", indent: 0pt, body-indent: 1.4em, spacing: sp * 0.25, number-align: left)
194 show enum: set text(..tabular)
195
196 set terms(separator: linebreak(), indent: 0pt, hanging-indent: sp * 1.5, spacing: sp * 0.6)
197 show terms: set par(first-line-indent: 0pt)
198 show terms.item: it => block(above: sp * 0.6, below: 0pt, {
199 block(below: 0pt, text(font: sans, size: sm, weight: 600, it.term))
200 block(inset: (left: sp * 1.5), it.description)
201 })
202
203// @e
204 // ── Tables ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
205 // Rules, not grids: a rule above the header, below the header, below the body.
206
207// @s tables
208 set table(
209 stroke: (x, y) => (bottom: if y == 0 { 1pt + rule-strong } else { 0.5pt + rule-color }),
210 inset: (left: 0pt, right: 0.7em, top: 0.45em, bottom: 0.45em),
211 align: left + horizon,
212 )
213 show table: set text(font: sans, size: sm, ..tabular)
214 show table: set par(justify: false, leading: leading-for(1.35), first-line-indent: 0pt)
215 show table.cell.where(y: 0): set text(size: xs, weight: 600, fill: ink-muted, tracking: 0.07em)
216 show table.cell.where(y: 0): upper
217
218// @e
219 // ── Figures & captions ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
220
221// @s figures
222 show figure: set block(above: sp * 1.5, below: sp * 1.5, breakable: false)
223 show figure.caption: it => block(
224 width: 100%,
225 inset: (top: 0.4em),
226 stroke: (top: 0.5pt + rule-color),
227 {
228 set text(font: sans, size: sm, fill: ink-muted)
229 set par(justify: false, leading: leading-for(1.4), first-line-indent: 0pt)
230 align(left, [#text(fill: ink, weight: 600, tracking: 0.06em, ..smcp)[#it.supplement #context it.counter.display()] — #it.body])
231 },
232 )
233
234// @e
235 // ── Code ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
236
237// @s codeblock
238 show raw: set text(font: mono, size: 0.86em, features: (liga: 0))
239 show raw.where(block: false): box.with(fill: wash, inset: (x: 0.28em), outset: (y: 0.1em), radius: 2pt)
240 show raw.where(block: true): it => block(
241 width: 100%,
242 fill: wash,
243 stroke: (left: 2pt + rule-strong),
244 inset: (x: 1em, y: 0.8em),
245 above: sp * 1.25,
246 below: sp * 1.25,
247 breakable: true,
248 { set text(size: 0.773em); set par(leading: leading-for(1.45), justify: false); it },
249 )
250
251// @e
252 // ── Inline ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
253
254// @s inline
255 show strong: set text(weight: 600)
256 show link: it => underline(offset: 0.14em, stroke: 0.5pt, it)
257 show footnote: set text(fill: accent, size: 0.7em, ..lining)
258 set footnote.entry(separator: line(length: 30%, stroke: 0.5pt + rule-color))
259 show footnote.entry: set text(size: sm)
260
261// @e
262
263 // Running heads and folios still span the full text width; only the flow is
264 // constrained. The block is breakable, so pagination is unaffected.
265 if measure == none { doc } else { block(width: measure, doc) }
266}
267
268// ── Blocks the spec names but no engine provides ────────────────────────────
269
270#let quotes-epigraph(attribution: none, body) = context {
271 let u = text.size
272 block(above: 0pt, below: u * 2, width: 24em, {
273 set align(left)
274 set text(size: u * 0.91, style: "italic", fill: ink-muted)
275 set par(justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt)
276 body
277 if attribution != none {
278 block(above: u * 0.5, text(style: "normal", size: u * 0.86)[— #attribution])
279 }
280 })
281}
282#let epigraph-right(attribution: none, body) = align(right, quotes-epigraph(attribution: attribution, body))
283
284#let quotes-pullquote(body) = context {
285 let u = text.size
286 block(
287 above: u * 1.5, below: u * 1.5, width: 100%,
288 inset: (y: u),
289 stroke: (top: 1.5pt + rule-strong, bottom: 0.5pt + rule-color),
290 {
291 set text(font: sans, size: u * 1.36, weight: 300)
292 set par(leading: leading-for(1.3), justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt)
293 align(center, body)
294 },
295 )
296}
297
298#let quotes-verse(body) = block(
299 above: sp * 1.25, below: sp * 1.25,
300 inset: (left: sp * 2),
301 {
302 set par(justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt, hanging-indent: 1.5em)
303 body
304 },
305)
306
307// @s callouts
308#let callouts-callout(title: none, warning: false, body) = context {
309 let u = text.size
310 block(
311 above: u * 1.25, below: u * 1.25, width: 100%,
312 fill: wash,
313 stroke: (
314 rest: 0.5pt + rule-color,
315 left: 2.5pt + (if warning { accent } else { rule-strong }),
316 ),
317 inset: (x: 1em, y: 0.75em),
318 breakable: false,
319 {
320 set text(size: u * 0.91)
321 if title != none {
322 block(below: 0.35em, text(
323 font: sans, size: u * 0.73, weight: 700, tracking: 0.09em,
324 fill: if warning { accent } else { ink-muted },
325 upper(title),
326 ))
327 }
328 body
329 },
330 )
331}
332// @e
333
334// Section breaks. A blank line cannot survive a page break, so the mark is
335// always visible. The spec names four registers, so there are four symbols
336// here — a caller should not have to know a string literal to pick one.
337// @s breaks
338#let _break-mark(mark, size: 10pt, tracking: 0em, color: ink-faint) = block(
339 above: sp * 1.5, below: sp * 1.5, sticky: true, width: 100%,
340 align(center, box(text(size: size, fill: color, tracking: tracking, mark))),
341)
342
343#let breaks-asterisks() = _break-mark([\* \* \*], tracking: 0.6em)
344#let breaks-asterism() = _break-mark([⁂], size: 14pt)
345#let breaks-fleuron() = _break-mark([❦], size: 12pt, color: accent)
346#let breaks-rule() = block(above: sp * 1.5, below: sp * 1.5, sticky: true, width: 100%,
347 align(center, line(length: 100%, stroke: 0.5pt + rule-color)))
348// @e
349
350// Drop cap. Typst has no float, so the spec's three-line wrap is NOT
351// expressible here: text cannot flow around a raised initial. Two honest
352// options, and one trap:
353// * `dropcap` below sets the initial in the margin — a marginal initial. The
354// measure stays intact and the opening still gets its signal.
355// * The `droplet` package implements a true wrap by measuring lines. Use it
356// where the three-line wrap is required rather than approximated.
357// * Do NOT put the cap and the paragraph in a two-column grid: that narrows
358// the entire opening paragraph, not just its first three lines.
359// @s dropcap
360#let dropcap(body) = {
361 let letters = body.text
362 let initial = letters.first()
363 let rest = letters.slice(1)
364 block(above: 0pt, {
365 place(
366 left,
367 dx: -1.35em,
368 dy: -0.08em,
369 text(size: 3.05em, fill: accent, top-edge: "cap-height", bottom-edge: "baseline")[#initial],
370 )
371 par(first-line-indent: 0pt)[#rest]
372 })
373}
374// @e
375
376// A table that fills the measure and closes with a strong rule. Typst's stroke
377// function cannot see the row count, so it is passed in.
378#let ts-table(columns: none, rows: none, ..cells) = {
379 table(
380 columns: columns,
381 stroke: (x, y) => (bottom: if y == 0 or y == rows { 1pt + rule-strong } else { 0.5pt + rule-color }),
382 ..cells,
383 )
384}

386// @s two-column
387// Two columns, equal. Papers, journal articles, newsletters, technical notes.
388//
389// `front` is set full width before the columns begin — a title block, an
390// abstract, a level-1 heading. Everything in `doc` flows in two columns.
391//
392// Typst's own `page(columns: 2)` fixes the gutter at 4% of the page width
393// (8.4mm on A4). The spec says 6mm, so the body goes through `columns()`
394// instead, which takes an explicit gutter and still breaks across pages.
395#let two-column(
396 front: none,
397 column-rule: false,
398 justified: true,
399 numbered: false,
400 running-head: true,
401 folio: true,
402 doc,
403) = {
404 // Justification is not optional at a 47-character measure.
405 assert(justified, message: "two-column requires justification: at 47 characters a ragged edge serrates the column")
406
407 show: typeset.with(
408 scale: scale-two-column,
409 measure: none, // the column is the measure
410 justified: true,
411 indented: true, // a blank line costs 3% of a column
412 numbered: numbered,
413 running-head: running-head,
414 folio: folio,
415 )
416
417 if front != none {
418 front
419 v(scale-two-column.space, weak: true)
420 }
421
422 // A hairline where the columns need separating. Most journals omit it — the
423 // gutter is already doing the work. `columns()` has no rule of its own, so it
424 // is drawn on the page behind the text, at the centre of the gutter. The
425 // offset flips with page parity because the margins mirror for duplex.
426 if column-rule {
427 set page(background: context {
428 let inner = if calc.odd(here().page()) { 28mm } else { 22mm }
429 place(
430 top + left,
431 dx: inner + 77mm + 3mm,
432 dy: 25mm,
433 line(angle: 90deg, length: 247mm, stroke: 0.5pt + rule-color),
434 )
435 })
436 }
437
438 columns(2, gutter: 6mm, doc)
439}
440
441// A level-1 heading spans both columns, which in Typst means it must be a
442// parent-scoped float. That works in `front`, before the columns begin. A
443// level-1 heading in the BODY has to be wrapped in `span()` explicitly —
444// Typst cannot promote it out of the column flow on its own. In a paper the
445// body's section headings are level 2 anyway; level 1 is the title.
446//
447// Spans both columns. A spanning element costs a break in both, so it is opt-in
448// per instance and must sit at the top or the bottom of the page — never
449// mid-column, which makes the reader find their place twice.
450#let span(body, at-bottom: false) = place(
451 if at-bottom { bottom } else { top },
452 scope: "parent",
453 float: true,
454 block(width: 100%, body),
455)

458// ── Front matter ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

460// @s frontmatter
461#let frontmatter-title-block(title: none, subtitle: none, author: none, place-date: none) = context {
462 let u = text.size
463 block(
464 below: u * 3, width: 100%,
465 inset: (bottom: u),
466 stroke: (bottom: 0.5pt + rule-color),
467 {
468 set par(justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt)

470 if subtitle != none {
471 block(below: u, text(font: sans, size: u * 1.27, weight: 300, fill: ink-muted, subtitle))
472 }
473 if author != none { text(tracking: 0.08em, ..smcp, author) }
474 if place-date != none {
475 block(above: 0.2em, text(font: sans, size: u * 0.86, fill: ink-muted, place-date))
476 }
477 },
478 )
479}

481
482#let frontmatter-abstract(width: 30em, body) = context {
483 let u = text.size
484 block(below: u * 2, width: width, {
485 set text(size: u * 0.91, fill: ink-muted)
486 set par(justify: false, leading: leading-for(1.45), first-line-indent: 0pt)
487 block(below: 0.3em, text(font: sans, size: u * 0.73, weight: 700, tracking: 0.1em, fill: ink-faint)[ABSTRACT])
488 body
489 })
490}
491
492#let frontmatter-colophon(body) = context {

497 stroke: (top: 0.5pt + rule-color),

501 body

511 margin: (top: 32mm, bottom: 28mm, x: 25mm),
512 header: none,
513 footer: none,
514 )
515 doc
516}

518
519// The sender block is address data, not a masthead: one style throughout, at
520// body size, in the reading face. Nothing bold, nothing in the sans.
521#let letter-sender(body) = context {
522 let u = text.size

524 set par(justify: false, leading: leading-for(1.35), first-line-indent: 0pt)
525 body

530// date, so it takes no gap of its own.
531#let letter-date-note(body) = context {

539#let letter-address-block(label: none, body) = block(below: sp * 1.5, {
540 set par(justify: false, leading: leading-for(1.35), first-line-indent: 0pt)
541 if label != none {
542 block(below: 0.25em, text(font: sans, size: xs, tracking: 0.1em, fill: ink-faint, upper(label)))
543 }
544 body
545})
546
547// The typed name, with room above it to sign. No rule: a ruled line is a form
548// to be filled in, and this is a letter.
549#let letter-signature(name) = context {
550 let u = text.size
551 block(above: u * 3, breakable: false, {
552 set par(justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt)
553 name
554 })
555}
556
557// "Enc." introduces a sentence; it does not head a section.
558#let letter-enclosures(body) = context {
559 let u = text.size
560 block(above: u * 2, {
561 set par(justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt)
562 [Enc. ]
563 body
564 })
565}
566
567// A postscript is a sentence that happens to begin with "P.S." — the label is
568// not a heading, so it matches the text it introduces exactly.
569#let letter-postscript(body) = context {
570 let u = text.size
571 block(above: u, {
572 set par(justify: false, first-line-indent: 0pt)
573 [P.S. ]
574 body
575 })
576}

602// ── Utilities ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
603
604// @s utilities
605#let utilities-keep-together(body) = block(breakable: false, body)
606#let utilities-tie(body) = box(body)
607// @e
